findings.conclusion: Both callsites pass only the newly created held output memfd after root ownership, size/type, tag, mode and required seals have been checked. The peer supplies neither the file handle nor mount descriptor. The helper is not a general authority validator by itself.

Only actual source F_GETFL with O_NOFOLLOW uses the handle helper. Error returns do not enter the ordinary proc-fd path or clear the bit. The old non-NOFOLLOW path is preserved. Fd and Descriptor reset/destruction preserve errno and close held output/readable/canonical/directory descriptors on unsuccessful returns.

The helper uses fixed 128-byte storage with explicit 8-byte ABI header/static layout checks, rejects empty/overbound/negative-type output, and passes the same held output descriptor into both syscalls. Original status flags plus CLOEXEC are submitted; final real F_GETFL must still equal the source flags. No capability, credential, namespace, security setting or fallback change appears in the delta.

The unchanged final checks revalidate the same backing inode, root ownership, mode/link/size, seals, exact status/CLOEXEC/zero offset/tag and live authority before release. The role path still completes FinishCreate and closes/revokes on its failure.
